wacc.formula: WACC = wₑ × kₑ + w_d × k_d × (1 − t);  kₑ = r_f + β × ERP

methods.formula: Value per share = (revenue in year 5 × target margin × (1 − tax) × exit P/E) ÷ (1 + kₑ + stage premium)^5 ÷ diluted shares
steps: Range: P/E 13.2x at a hurdle 2.5 points higher → $1.72; P/E 48.6x at 2.5 points lower → $7.87
inputs: SEC XBRL frames: diluted weighted-average shares
assumptions: its own growth fading to terminal (the DCF's path)
peer P/E, SIC 283 (Pharmaceutical Preparations), revenue under $1B (143 observations)
cost of equity 9.8% + 5% stage premium (an assumption)
methods.fit: It is not yet profitable (−$159.8M operating income, revenue growth 449%), so its value lies in what it can earn once it matures.

methods.formula: ln(EV/Sales) = a + b × (revenue growth + free-cash-flow margin); value per share = (fitted EV/Sales × revenue − net debt) ÷ shares
inputs: last four quarters vs the four before
assumptions: every covered non-financial company with revenue ≥ $50M, today
methods.fit: At the pre-profit / high growth stage, growth and cash generation drive the price: its Rule of 40 score is 266 (growth 449% + free-cash-flow margin -183%).

methods.formula: Value per share = (1 − p) × going-concern value + p × liquidation value
steps: p(fail within 5 years) = clamp(0.5 − runway 1.0 years ÷ 10, 5%, 50%) = 40.5%
inputs: SEC XBRL frames: diluted weighted-average shares
assumptions: no distress estimate: from the cash runway (an assumption)
an assumption for a forced sale
methods.fit: It is burning cash (free cash flow −$159.8M a year, a runway of 1.0 years), so its value must allow for the chance it does not survive.

methods.formula: Stage-weighted value = Σ weight × central value of the stage's methods (weights renormalized over the methods available)
steps: 25% × −$0.28 (Path-to-margin DCF, dilution-adjusted) + 20% × −$0.01 (Survival-weighted value) + 20% × $2.97 (Exit-multiple (venture) method) + 15% × $3.08 (EV/Sales vs Rule of 40 (all-company fit)) + 20% × $5.17 (EV/Sales vs peers) = $2.02
assumptions: fixed by stage before any result was seen (base_rates.STAGES)
methods.fit: Its stage is “Pre-profit / high growth” — operating income ≤ 0, revenue growth +448.8% — which fixes these methods and their weights in advance.

methods.formula: Net current asset value per share = (current assets − total liabilities − other claims) ÷ shares;  a net-net trades below two-thirds of it
inputs: SEC XBRL frames: diluted weighted-average shares
assumptions: Fixed assets, goodwill, the business itself
Graham, Security Analysis (1934): a liquidation floor
methods.fit: Its current assets and liabilities are on file. Net-nets are rare among large companies; a positive figure is a floor that ignores everything the business owns beyond working capital.

methods.formula: ln(EV/Sales) = a + b₁ × growth + b₂ × ln(operating margin, at least 0.5%) + b₃ × loss flag + b₄ × ln(revenue, $B) + sector effect;  value = (fitted EV/Sales × revenue − net debt) ÷ shares
inputs: last four quarters vs the four before
assumptions: every covered non-financial company with revenue ≥ $50M, today; ridge λ = 1
methods.fit: It is a non-financial company with revenue on file, so the multiple the market pays companies with its growth, margin, size and sector applies.

methods.formula: Value = (assets in place + C − net debt) ÷ shares;  C = S·N(d₁) − K·e^(−rT)·N(d₂), d₁ = [ln(S ÷ K) + (r + σ²/2)T] ÷ σ√T, d₂ = d₁ − σ√T
steps: S = the expansion in year 5: the revenue it adds $320.1M (to $407.6M) × margin 15.0% × (1 − tax), as a growing perpetuity, discounted = $278.0M
K = capital to build it: $320.1M ÷ sales-to-capital 1.50 = $213.4M
σ = 75% (its stock, a year of daily closes), T = 5 years, r = 4.91% → C = $192.7M
assets in place = NOPAT −$126.2M ÷ WACC = $0; value = ($0 + $192.7M + net cash $152.5M) ÷ 100,116,000 = $3.45
assumptions: an assumption: the business is riskier than the market sees only through its price
Return on new capital in perpetuity
methods.fit: It is loss-making or growing fast: much of its value is the chance to become a larger, profitable business, which behaves like an option — worth more the more uncertain it is.
